set.approach: From the Conrad Kain hut or Applebee campground, walk north on the trail toward the Bugaboo-Snowpatch Col, leaving it short of the col on the line to Crescent Spire; from Applebee, go north onto the moraine and take that same line. This reaches the Crescent Glacier, and the east face is obvious from both approaches. The face is steep and nearly blank, with only a handful of routes on it.
set.descent_text: The usual way down from the spire is the Kain Route, which parties use as the descent for every route on the mountain. From the summit it leads down the ridge on the Kain hut side of the peak, with rappels off the south summit and from the gendarme on its east side rather than the side you would expect, then a stretch of fourth-class ridge and the chimneys above the Bugaboo-Snowpatch Col. Stay on the hut side of the ridge crest and keep well to skier's right near the bottom, whatever the old trails and cairns suggest.

review.notes: Area page gives the approach to the east face via the Crescent Glacier and states the Kain Route is the descent for all routes on the spire; Kain route detail from the same page. Top-out of this particular line not stated, so medium.

set.approach: The main approach goes from the Kain hut or Applebee campground over the Bugaboo-Snowpatch Col, then northwest down the Vowell Glacier beneath the north ridge to the North Shoulder Col. Descend west into the steep, loose gully, skirt the small glacier below the northwest face on its right, and scree and glacier lead south to the foot of the west face. The alternative is the East Creek basin: take the ridge toward the middle tower, then rappel to the glacier below and cross the cirque. Either way is long and remote, with rockfall off the north face above the cirque. The route starts from the ledges where the lower wall pushes furthest into the glacier.
set.descent_text: The route ends on the summit ridge, a long stretch of fourth-class climbing with the odd harder move. The descent is by rappel down the east face, on anchors that range from pitons to slung horns and shift from year to year; the rock is very loose. Below the bergschrund, rappel or downclimb to the glacier, avoiding crevasses, and walk out.

review.notes: Route page gives the start, East Basin approach and east-face rappel descent; area page gives the North Shoulder Col approach; Seventh Rifle page confirms the east-face descent and loose rock. Rappel counts left out because the pages disagree.

set.approach: The main approach goes from the Kain hut or Applebee campground over the Bugaboo-Snowpatch Col, then northwest down the Vowell Glacier beneath the north ridge to the North Shoulder Col. Descend west into the steep, loose gully, skirt the small glacier below the northwest face on its right, and scree and glacier lead south to the foot of the west face. The East Creek basin is the other way in, with bolted rappels down to the base. Look for a corner crack that is wide at the back and has a hand-width splitter on its right side, a little left of where the west face comes lowest.
set.descent_text: The route ends on the summit ridge. The descent is by rappel down the east face just below the summit, to below the bergschrund and then a short downclimb to the glacier. The east face is very loose, the old rappel anchors may need replacing, and ropes can snag.

review.notes: Start, East Creek approach and east-face descent from the route page; North Shoulder Col approach from the area page; descent corroborated by the Watchtower page. Rappel count omitted (pages disagree).
